searchText: it's not my place to say yay or nay for consolidations as a concept, but in terms on complexity it seems straight forward for the EL to accumulate consolidation requests and send them over to the CL via the engine api yeah I meant that you seemed to agree with my assessment of complexity yep just wanted to make sure my post was only taken under that context 👍 On the EL, I'm trying to convert all EL->CL messages to a similar data type so it is even easier for us to integrate these types of things going forward https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8432 i have a similar assessment (from ethereumjs prespective), that complexity is only incremental w.r.t. 7002 so imo we SHOULD do EL triggered consolidations the current specs are/were confused about `MAX_EXECUTION_LAYER_EXITS_PER_PAYLOAD` vs `MAX_EXECUTION_LAYER_EXITS` -- was that fixed somewhere? for 7002 in CL if we are referring to the same thing then yes latest spec is on `dev` now https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/electra/beacon-chain.md#execution there is the constant `MAX_WITHDRAWAL_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD` now <@199561711278227457> https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/pectra-devnet-0# could the prysm columns for 7002 and 7549 be updated to the building icon? ok, it's `PER_PAYLOAD` also I tried editing https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/pectra-devnet-0 for Nimbus but some login issue, but basically 6110 in progress, 7002 should be on its way to merging, the EL-only ones obviously not relevant to `nimbus-eth2`, and remaining 7251/7549 outstanding/not yet started right, this is referring to the cap on messages coming from the EL right, the semantics I understand, it's just that at least at the commithash I was looking at, the same constant has `FOO` and `FOO_PER_PAYLOAD` names depending on where one looks I also tried to login, but seems I have no permissions to edit. Grandine started to work on all four EIP-6110, EIP-7002, EIP-7251, EIP-7549.
